items.title: Locating Target Objects
items.description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
items.content: Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

items.title: Sequential Object Placement
items.description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
items.content: Follow a consistent workflow: identify the object's location, retrieve the object, navigate to the designated destination, and then execute the placement action.

items.title: Cleaning before Storage

items.content: Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

items.title: Systematic Exploration for Objects
items.description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
items.content: Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

items.title: Container Interaction Workflow
items.description: Use whenever an object must be placed into or retrieved from a storage unit.
items.content: Always ensure the target container is open before attempting to move an object into or out of it. After completing the placement, remember to close the container to restore the scene's state and complete the task properly.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

---
name: Container Interaction Workflow
description: Use whenever an object must be placed into or retrieved from a storage unit.
---
Always ensure the target container is open before attempting to move an object into or out of it. After completing the placement, remember to close the container to restore the scene's state and complete the task properly.

memory_context:
---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

---
name: Sequential Object Placement
description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---
Follow a consistent workflow: identify the object's location, retrieve the object, navigate to the designated destination, and then execute the placement action.

---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---
Before moving to a destination, use inventory checks to verify current holdings. Utilize examination actions on source containers to confirm whether additional target objects remain to be picked up, ensuring no items are missed during the collection process.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

items.content: Simply placing an object inside an appliance is not sufficient to change its state. You must actively operate the appliance (e.g., turn it on) to apply the heat or cooling effect required to meet the task criteria.

items.title: Sequential Goal Execution
items.description: Use this when a task involves both transforming an object and moving it to a destination.
items.content: Break the task into logical phases: acquire the object, perform the transformation (heating/cooling), and finally transport it to the goal location. Ensure the ultimate destination is not ignored after the transformation step is complete.

items.title: Loop Detection and Reassessment
items.description: Use this when you find yourself repeatedly executing the same actions (e.g., opening and closing a door) without observing a change in the object's properties or the task's status.
items.content: If repetition does not progress the task, stop and re-evaluate the sequence; you are likely missing a required step, such as turning on an appliance, or using the wrong appliance for the intended transformation.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---
Start by inspecting closed containers like drawers or cabinets where items are frequently stored. If the target is not found in these containers, expand the search to open surface areas such as tables or shelves, which are alternative locations for small items.

---
name: Selecting from Multiple Candidates
description: Use this strategy when your scan identifies multiple instances of the requested object.
---
If the environment contains multiple units of the required item, any single instance is sufficient to complete the task. Select the most accessible unit to minimize movement and reduce the number of actions required.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

---
name: Container Interaction Workflow
description: Use whenever an object must be placed into or retrieved from a storage unit.
---
Always ensure the target container is open before attempting to move an object into or out of it. After completing the placement, remember to close the container to restore the scene's state and complete the task properly.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---
Before moving to a destination, use inventory checks to verify current holdings. Utilize examination actions on source containers to confirm whether additional target objects remain to be picked up, ensuring no items are missed during the collection process.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Prioritize searching inside closed containers like drawers or cabinets first. If the target object is not found in these storage areas, systematically shift the search to open surface areas, such as countertops or tables, where objects are frequently left exposed.

items.title: Systematic Exhaustive Search
items.description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
items.content: Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. items.title: Redundant Visit Avoidance
items.description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Prioritize searching inside closed containers like drawers or cabinets first. If the target object is not found in these storage areas, systematically shift the search to open surface areas, such as countertops or tables, where objects are frequently left exposed.

---
name: Target-Oriented Object Relocation
description: Use this process once the required object has been successfully located and acquired.
---
After picking up the required object, navigate directly to the designated destination location. Complete the task by performing a placement action to move the held object onto or into the target receptacle or surface.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---

---
name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---
Start by inspecting closed containers like drawers or cabinets where items are frequently stored. If the target is not found in these containers, expand the search to open surface areas such as tables or shelves, which are alternative locations for small items.

---
name: Selecting from Multiple Candidates
description: Use this strategy when your scan identifies multiple instances of the requested object.
---
If the environment contains multiple units of the required item, any single instance is sufficient to complete the task. Select the most accessible unit to minimize movement and reduce the number of actions required.

---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

---
name: Sequential Object Placement
description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---
Follow a consistent workflow: identify the object's location, retrieve the object, navigate to the designated destination, and then execute the placement action.

---
name: Cooling Items
description: Use when the task requirement involves "cool [object]".
---
To cool an object, you must place it inside a fridge to change its state. Do not assume that randomly found objects are already at the required temperature; always locate and utilize a fridge to perform the cooling action before attempting to complete the task.

items.title: Systematic Exploration Strategy
items.description: Use this strategy when searching for an object that is not immediately visible in the environment.
items.content: Instead of repeatedly checking a small subset of locations, generate a checklist of all potential receptacles (e.g., tables, cabinets, drawers, surfaces) identified in the initial room observation and visit each one methodically until the target object is located.

items.title: Prevent Repetitive Search Cycles
items.description: Use this when navigating a room to find an object to avoid getting stuck in infinite loops.
items.content: Maintain a record of locations already searched; if you find yourself visiting the same sequence of furniture multiple times without success, force a change in strategy and pivot to exploring previously unvisited areas of the room.

items.title: Broaden Search Scope to All Surfaces
items.description: Use this when you cannot locate a specific item in expected storage containers.
items.content: If the target object is not found in primary storage locations like drawers or cabinets, expand the search to all available surfaces mentioned in the scene, such as tables, chairs, beds, or floors. memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

---
name: Sequential Object Placement
description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---
Follow a consistent workflow: identify the object's location, retrieve the object, navigate to the designated destination, and then execute the placement action.

---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

---
name: Sequential Object Placement
description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---
Follow a consistent workflow: identify the object's location, retrieve the object, navigate to the designated destination, and then execute the placement action.

---
name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---
Start by inspecting closed containers like drawers or cabinets where items are frequently stored. If the target is not found in these containers, expand the search to open surface areas such as tables or shelves, which are alternative locations for small items.

items.title: Avoid Redundant Searches
items.description: Use this when conducting a search in an environment with multiple containers to prevent wasted actions.
items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit list of all containers that have already been opened and inspected. Never revisit a container that has previously been verified as empty, as repeating these actions does not provide new information and hinders progress.

items.title: Prioritize Surface Scanning
items.description: Use this when the target object is not immediately visible and you need to determine where to search first.
items.content: Always visually inspect open surfaces (like dining tables or countertops) before interacting with closed containers (like cabinets or drawers). Open surfaces can be surveyed without additional interaction steps, making them the most efficient locations to check for the target object.

items.title: Systematic Search Pathing
items.description: Use this to ensure complete coverage of a room when the location of an object is unknown.
items.content: Organize your search by grouping similar furniture types (e.g., all cabinets together, then all drawers) and progress through them in a linear, logical order. This prevents aimless wandering and ensures that every potential location is checked exactly once, reducing the likelihood of skipping areas or falling into unproductive movement loops.

memory_context:
---
name: Recursive Object Searching
description: Use this strategy when the target items are not found on open surfaces or within primary storage locations like drawers.
---
If an initial scan of furniture surfaces and drawers fails to reveal the target, inspect the contents of containers (such as boxes, baskets, or cases) found on those surfaces, as they often contain hidden items.

---
name: Comprehensive Environmental Scanning
description: Use this when searching for items that are frequently misplaced on furniture rather than stored in containers.
---
Expand the search scope to include all furniture surfaces, such as beds, chairs, and tables, as items are often placed on top of these objects rather than exclusively inside designated storage units.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when an initial sweep of a room's storage locations fails to locate the target objects.
---
Maintain a log of inspected areas to prevent repeating visits to the exact same containers, and instead pivot to checking entirely new locations or categories of furniture if the current search strategy proves unproductive.

---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

---
name: Container Interaction Workflow
description: Use whenever an object must be placed into or retrieved from a storage unit.
---
Always ensure the target container is open before attempting to move an object into or out of it. After completing the placement, remember to close the container to restore the scene's state and complete the task properly.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Prioritize searching inside closed containers like drawers or cabinets first. If the target object is not found in these storage areas, systematically shift the search to open surface areas, such as countertops or tables, where objects are frequently left exposed.

---
name: Target-Oriented Object Relocation
description: Use this process once the required object has been successfully located and acquired.
---
After picking up the required object, navigate directly to the designated destination location. Complete the task by performing a placement action to move the held object onto or into the target receptacle or surface.

items.title: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
items.description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
items.content: Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

items.title: Systematic Search Expansion
items.description: Use this strategy when an initial search of nearby containers fails to yield the target object.
items.content: Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---
Before moving to a destination, use inventory checks to verify current holdings. Utilize examination actions on source containers to confirm whether additional target objects remain to be picked up, ensuring no items are missed during the collection process.

---
name: Recursive Object Searching
description: Use this strategy when the target items are not found on open surfaces or within primary storage locations like drawers.
---
If an initial scan of furniture surfaces and drawers fails to reveal the target, inspect the contents of containers (such as boxes, baskets, or cases) found on those surfaces, as they often contain hidden items.

---
name: Comprehensive Environmental Scanning
description: Use this when searching for items that are frequently misplaced on furniture rather than stored in containers.
---
Expand the search scope to include all furniture surfaces, such as beds, chairs, and tables, as items are often placed on top of these objects rather than exclusively inside designated storage units.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when an initial sweep of a room's storage locations fails to locate the target objects.
---
Maintain a log of inspected areas to prevent repeating visits to the exact same containers, and instead pivot to checking entirely new locations or categories of furniture if the current search strategy proves unproductive.

name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

---
name: Sequential Object Placement
description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---

---
name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---

---
name: Selecting from Multiple Candidates
description: Use this strategy when your scan identifies multiple instances of the requested object.
---
If the environment contains multiple units of the required item, any single instance is sufficient to complete the task. Select the most accessible unit to minimize movement and reduce the number of actions required.

---
name: Systematic Exploration Strategy
description: Use this strategy when searching for an object that is not immediately visible in the environment.
---

memory_context:
---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

---
name: Sequential Handling of Multiple Items
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same object type to a single destination.
---
Perform the pickup and placement actions for each individual item in a complete cycle (pick up, move, deposit) until the total required count of items has been successfully transferred to the target location.

---
name: Locating Target Objects in Bulk
description: Use this strategy when you need to collect multiple items to fulfill a placement task.
---
Before starting, scan the environment for surfaces or containers that hold multiple instances of the required object type; navigating to a location containing multiple targets minimizes the number of travel actions needed to gather all items.

---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

items.title: Parsing Spatial Constraints in Tasks
items.description: Use this strategy when a task instruction specifies a spatial relationship (e.g., "under", "next to", "inside") between two objects.
items.content: Do not assume that performing an action on the target object alone is sufficient. You must explicitly identify both the target object and the reference (landmark) object in the environment, then manipulate the target object to align with the specified spatial constraint relative to the reference object.

items.title: Verifying Environmental Preconditions
items.description: Use this strategy when an instruction requires examining an object under specific environmental conditions, such as a particular light source.
items.content: Do not merely execute an "examine" or "look" command on the target object if the task involves environmental factors. First, locate and activate the necessary utility (e.g., turning on a light source), then ensure the target object is positioned within the active field of that utility before performing the observation action.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

---
name: Locating Hidden Objects
description: Use this procedure when the required item is not present in the immediate surroundings.
---
Systematically check potential storage areas such as cabinets and drawers. Remember to open closed containers to inspect their contents thoroughly before moving to the next location.

---
name: Heating Objects
description: Use this procedure when a task specifically requires an object to be heated before it is placed at the final destination.
---
Place the target object inside an appropriate heating appliance, operate the device to perform the heating action, and then retrieve the object from the appliance before attempting to transport it to the target location.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
---
Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---

---
name: Sequential Handling of Multiple Items
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same object type to a single destination.
---
Perform the pickup and placement actions for each individual item in a complete cycle (pick up, move, deposit) until the total required count of items has been successfully transferred to the target location.

---
name: Locating Target Objects in Bulk
description: Use this strategy when you need to collect multiple items to fulfill a placement task.
---
Before starting, scan the environment for surfaces or containers that hold multiple instances of the required object type; navigating to a location containing multiple targets minimizes the number of travel actions needed to gather all items.

---
name: Locating Target Objects
description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---
Systematically inspect nearby furniture and storage surfaces, such as shelves, counters, or basins, to find and retrieve necessary items before navigating to the target location.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

---
name: Broaden Search Locations for Common Objects
description: Use this strategy when a required object is not found in the primary set of containers initially searched.
---
If common household items (like plates or cups) are not found in cabinets or drawers, do not limit future searches to those same types of containers. Expand the search to include other logical locations such as dishwashers, open shelves, dining tables, or surfaces where items might have been left.

---
name: Maintain Search State to Avoid Redundant Loops
description: Use this strategy during long-running tasks involving repetitive searching of multiple containers.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected to prevent entering an infinite loop of re-visiting the same locations. If an exhaustive search of all accessible containers fails, stop repeating the search cycle and re-evaluate the environment to look for missed locations or alternative strategies.

---
name: Validate Object Availability via Scene Inspection
description: Use this strategy before initiating an exhaustive search for an object.
---
Carefully scan the initial room observation provided at the start of the task to determine if the target object exists in the environment. Do not blindly search containers if there is no indication that the object is present; prioritize identifying the object's presence or logical location based on the initial scene description.

items.title: Systematic Search Strategy
items.description: Use when attempting to locate a specific object within an environment containing many potential storage locations.
items.content: Instead of searching randomly or repeating checks on the same locations, proceed with a structured search pattern (e.g., scanning all storage units in a specific order, such as left-to-right or by proximity). items.title: Track Visited Locations
items.description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.
items.content: Maintain a mental or list-based log of containers that have already been opened and inspected. Avoid wasting time re-opening or re-visiting containers confirmed to be empty, and prioritize moving to unexplored areas to maximize search efficiency.

items.title: Exhaustive Exploration
items.description: Use when primary locations (like the first few drawers or countertops) do not contain the target object.
items.content: Do not prematurely conclude the search if the target is not in the most obvious locations. Systematically expand the search scope to include all available furniture (such as all cabinets and drawers) until the object is found, rather than returning to previously checked areas.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Prioritize searching inside closed containers like drawers or cabinets first. If the target object is not found in these storage areas, systematically shift the search to open surface areas, such as countertops or tables, where objects are frequently left exposed.

---
name: Target-Oriented Object Relocation
description: Use this process once the required object has been successfully located and acquired.
---
After picking up the required object, navigate directly to the designated destination location. Complete the task by performing a placement action to move the held object onto or into the target receptacle or surface.

---
name: Cooling Items
description: Use when the task requirement involves "cool [object]".
---
To cool an object, you must place it inside a fridge to change its state. Do not assume that randomly found objects are already at the required temperature; always locate and utilize a fridge to perform the cooling action before attempting to complete the task.

---
name: Action Sequence Planning
description: Use when a task requires multiple state changes (e.g., finding, then cooling, then placing).
---
Break complex tasks into distinct sub-goals: first retrieve the target object, then apply the necessary state transformations (like cooling in a fridge), and finally move the object to the destination. Do not attempt the final placement until the object satisfies all state constraints specified in the query.

---
name: Preventing Redundant Search Loops
description: Use when the agent is stuck repeatedly examining the same objects or visiting empty containers.
---
If you have already inspected a container and found it empty, mark it as searched and avoid revisiting it. If progress stalls, stop re-examining held items and focus on identifying which appliance is needed to modify the object's current state to meet the task's requirements.

items.title: Final Object Placement

name: Locating Target Objects in Bulk
description: Use this strategy when you need to collect multiple items to fulfill a placement task.
---
Before starting, scan the environment for surfaces or containers that hold multiple instances of the required object type; navigating to a location containing multiple targets minimizes the number of travel actions needed to gather all items.

---
name: Systematic Search Strategy
description: Apply this when searching for an object in an unknown location among multiple potential storage areas.
---
When a target object is missing from your initial viewpoint, systematically navigate to and inspect all candidate surfaces of the same category (e.g., all tables or drawers) one by one until the object is discovered. Do not prematurely assume the object is absent if only one location has been checked.

---
name: Efficient Object Transportation
description: Use this sequence when the goal is to transfer an object from a source to a destination.
---

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this when the location of the target object is unknown at the start of the task.
---
Sequentially navigate to and inspect potential support surfaces—such as tables, shelves, or counters—until the target object is identified, avoiding the assumption that the item is in a specific pre-determined location.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Prioritize High-Density Locations
description: When a task requires gathering multiple instances of the same object, use this strategy to minimize navigation.
---
If you encounter a location that contains multiple instances of the required target object, exhaust that location by collecting them one by one before searching elsewhere. This prevents unnecessary travel between different containers or surfaces.

---
name: Iterative Transport Strategy
description: Use this workflow when you must move multiple items to a single destination.
---
Instead of attempting to gather all items before moving, establish a repetitive loop: navigate to the source, pick up one instance of the object, move to the destination to deposit it, and return to the source. Repeat this sequence until the total required quantity is successfully transported.

---
name: Broaden Search Locations for Common Objects
description: Use this strategy when a required object is not found in the primary set of containers initially searched.
---
If common household items (like plates or cups) are not found in cabinets or drawers, do not limit future searches to those same types of containers. Expand the search to include other logical locations such as dishwashers, open shelves, dining tables, or surfaces where items might have been left.

items.title: Systematic Container Search
items.description: Use this strategy to avoid wasting moves by re-checking containers that have already been explored.
items.content: Track which containers you have already opened and inspected. If a container has been checked and found empty, mark it as searched and do not revisit it unless there is a specific reason to believe the object state has changed.

items.title: Expanding Search Scope
items.description: Use this when the initial set of containers is empty and you haven't found your target.
items.content: If you have exhausted common storage areas like cabinets, broaden your search to include other potential object receptacles such as ovens, drawers, or appliances, as items might be stored in less obvious places.

items.title: Avoiding Repetitive Trajectories
items.description: Use this to break out of inefficient search loops.
items.content: If you find yourself visiting the same locations repeatedly without finding the target, force a change in strategy by deliberately selecting a new, unexplored set of areas to inspect, rather than looping back to previously searched locations.

memory_context:
---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---
Before moving to a destination, use inventory checks to verify current holdings. Utilize examination actions on source containers to confirm whether additional target objects remain to be picked up, ensuring no items are missed during the collection process.

---
name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---
Start by inspecting closed containers like drawers or cabinets where items are frequently stored. If the target is not found in these containers, expand the search to open surface areas such as tables or shelves, which are alternative locations for small items.

---
name: Selecting from Multiple Candidates
description: Use this strategy when your scan identifies multiple instances of the requested object.
---
If the environment contains multiple units of the required item, any single instance is sufficient to complete the task. Select the most accessible unit to minimize movement and reduce the number of actions required.

---
name: Recursive Object Searching
description: Use this strategy when the target items are not found on open surfaces or within primary storage locations like drawers.
---
If an initial scan of furniture surfaces and drawers fails to reveal the target, inspect the contents of containers (such as boxes, baskets, or cases) found on those surfaces, as they often contain hidden items.

name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.

name: Systematic Search Expansion

---
Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

items.content: If the object is not found in the primary storage appliance, systematically search other furniture and open surfaces such as countertops until the item is identified and can be picked up.

items.title: Workflow for State-Modifying Tasks
items.description: Use this sequence when a task requires an object to be in a specific state before being placed at a destination.
items.content: Always acquire the target object first, perform the necessary state-change operation (such as cooling or heating) using the appropriate appliance, and only then move the object to the final destination.

## Content If the object is not found in the primary storage appliance, systematically search other furniture and open surfaces such as countertops until the item is identified and can be picked up.

# Memory Item 2
## Title Workflow for State-Modifying Tasks
## Description Use this sequence when a task requires an object to be in a specific state before being placed at a destination.
## Content Always acquire the target object first, perform the necessary state-change operation (such as cooling or heating) using the appropriate appliance, and only then move the object to the final destination.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search Strategy
description: Use when attempting to locate a specific object within an environment containing many potential storage locations.
---
Instead of searching randomly or repeating checks on the same locations, proceed with a structured search pattern (e.g., scanning all storage units in a specific order, such as left-to-right or by proximity). This ensures that every container is checked once before assuming the object is missing.

---
name: Track Visited Locations
description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.
---
Maintain a mental or list-based log of containers that have already been opened and inspected. Avoid wasting time re-opening or re-visiting containers confirmed to be empty, and prioritize moving to unexplored areas to maximize search efficiency.

---
name: Exhaustive Exploration
description: Use when primary locations (like the first few drawers or countertops) do not contain the target object.
---
Do not prematurely conclude the search if the target is not in the most obvious locations. Systematically expand the search scope to include all available furniture (such as all cabinets and drawers) until the object is found, rather than returning to previously checked areas.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

name: Systematic Exhaustive Search

description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.

---

description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.

name: Heating or Cooling Objects
description: Use this when a task requires an object to have a specific state (e.g., "hot," "chilled") before being placed in its final location.
---
Simply placing an object inside an appliance is not sufficient to change its state. You must actively operate the appliance (e.g., turn it on) to apply the heat or cooling effect required to meet the task criteria.

---
name: Sequential Goal Execution
description: Use this when a task involves both transforming an object and moving it to a destination.
---
Break the task into logical phases: acquire the object, perform the transformation (heating/cooling), and finally transport it to the goal location. Ensure the ultimate destination is not ignored after the transformation step is complete.

---
name: Loop Detection and Reassessment
description: Use this when you find yourself repeatedly executing the same actions (e.g., opening and closing a door) without observing a change in the object's properties or the task's status.
---
If repetition does not progress the task, stop and re-evaluate the sequence; you are likely missing a required step, such as turning on an appliance, or using the wrong appliance for the intended transformation.

---
name: Locating Hidden Objects
description: Use this procedure when the required item is not present in the immediate surroundings.
---
Systematically check potential storage areas such as cabinets and drawers. Remember to open closed containers to inspect their contents thoroughly before moving to the next location.

---
name: Heating Objects
description: Use this procedure when a task specifically requires an object to be heated before it is placed at the final destination.
---
Place the target object inside an appropriate heating appliance, operate the device to perform the heating action, and then retrieve the object from the appliance before attempting to transport it to the target location.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Prioritize High-Density Locations
description: When a task requires gathering multiple instances of the same object, use this strategy to minimize navigation.
---
If you encounter a location that contains multiple instances of the required target object, exhaust that location by collecting them one by one before searching elsewhere. This prevents unnecessary travel between different containers or surfaces.

---
name: Iterative Transport Strategy
description: Use this workflow when you must move multiple items to a single destination.
---
Instead of attempting to gather all items before moving, establish a repetitive loop: navigate to the source, pick up one instance of the object, move to the destination to deposit it, and return to the source. Repeat this sequence until the total required quantity is successfully transported.

---
name: Systematic Container Search
description: Use this strategy to avoid wasting moves by re-checking containers that have already been explored.
---
Track which containers you have already opened and inspected. If a container has been checked and found empty, mark it as searched and do not revisit it unless there is a specific reason to believe the object state has changed.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
---
Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

---
name: Systematic Search Expansion
description: Use this strategy when an initial search of nearby containers fails to yield the target object.
---
Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

---
name: Context-Aware Object Location
description: Use this strategy when searching for common household items that have specific state requirements (e.g., "clean").
---
If the object is not found in its typical storage location, broaden the search to include utility areas like sink basins or dish racks, as items may be located there waiting to be cleaned or dried. If the object is found in a dirty state, perform a cleaning action before proceeding with the rest of the task.

---
name: Handling Cleanliness Requirements
description: Use this when a task specifically requires an object to be in a "clean" state before placement.
---
Before placing an object at the target destination, check if it requires cleaning. If it is dirty or its status is unknown, navigate to a water source (such as a sink) to clean the object first, then proceed to the target location.

---
name: Prioritizing Surfaces in Search
description: Use this when searching for an object whose exact location is unknown.
---
Before exhaustively opening multiple storage containers like drawers or cabinets, first visually scan nearby surfaces like tables or countertops. Objects required for tasks are often already present on open surfaces, which is more efficient than checking multiple enclosed storage units.

items.title: Cleaning Objects Prior to Storage
items.description: Use this strategy when the task requires an object to be in a "clean" state before it is placed in its final storage location.
items.content: Do not assume that an object retrieved from a countertop or table is already clean. Navigate to a sink or water source and perform the cleaning action on the object immediately before moving it to the target container.

items.title: Managing Enclosed Storage
items.description: Use this strategy when the destination for an object is a closed storage container such as a drawer or cabinet.
items.content: Always verify if the target container is open before attempting to place an object inside. If it is closed, perform an open action first, then proceed with the storage action, and finish by closing the container.

memory_context:
---
name: Parsing Spatial Constraints in Tasks
description: Use this strategy when a task instruction specifies a spatial relationship (e.g., "under", "next to", "inside") between two objects.
---
Do not assume that performing an action on the target object alone is sufficient. You must explicitly identify both the target object and the reference (landmark) object in the environment, then manipulate the target object to align with the specified spatial constraint relative to the reference object.

---
name: Verifying Environmental Preconditions
description: Use this strategy when an instruction requires examining an object under specific environmental conditions, such as a particular light source.
---
Do not merely execute an "examine" or "look" command on the target object if the task involves environmental factors. First, locate and activate the necessary utility (e.g., turning on a light source), then ensure the target object is positioned within the active field of that utility before performing the observation action.

---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

---
name: Sequential Handling of Multiple Items
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same object type to a single destination.
---
Perform the pickup and placement actions for each individual item in a complete cycle (pick up, move, deposit) until the total required count of items has been successfully transferred to the target location.

---
name: Broaden Search Locations for Common Objects
description: Use this strategy when a required object is not found in the primary set of containers initially searched.
---
If common household items (like plates or cups) are not found in cabinets or drawers, do not limit future searches to those same types of containers. Expand the search to include other logical locations such as dishwashers, open shelves, dining tables, or surfaces where items might have been left.

---
name: Maintain Search State to Avoid Redundant Loops
description: Use this strategy during long-running tasks involving repetitive searching of multiple containers.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected to prevent entering an infinite loop of re-visiting the same locations. If an exhaustive search of all accessible containers fails, stop repeating the search cycle and re-evaluate the environment to look for missed locations or alternative strategies.

---
name: Validate Object Availability via Scene Inspection
description: Use this strategy before initiating an exhaustive search for an object.
---
Carefully scan the initial room observation provided at the start of the task to determine if the target object exists in the environment. Do not blindly search containers if there is no indication that the object is present; prioritize identifying the object's presence or logical location based on the initial scene description.

---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

items.description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

items.title: Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
items.description: Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
items.content: Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.

items.title: Task Termination upon Search Exhaustion
items.description: Use this strategy when all potential locations in the environment have been checked for the target object.
items.content: If every accessible container and surface has been searched and the target object is still not found, conclude the task execution rather than continuing to move. Recognizing when an object is unavailable prevents the agent from entering an infinite loop of redundant actions.

# Memory Item 1
## Title Systematic Search Coverage
## Description Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
## Content Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

# Memory Item 2
## Title Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
## Description Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
## Content Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.

# Memory Item 3
## Title Task Termination upon Search Exhaustion
## Description Use this strategy when all potential locations in the environment have been checked for the target object.
## Content If every accessible container and surface has been searched and the target object is still not found, conclude the task execution rather than continuing to move. Recognizing when an object is unavailable prevents the agent from entering an infinite loop of redundant actions.

name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.

name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Similar Containers
description: Use when target items are not immediately found in the first set of inspected containers like drawers or side tables.
---

name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles

---

name: Systematic Exploration of the Environment
description: Use this strategy when the initial search for target objects fails to yield results.
---
Instead of repeatedly visiting the same locations, perform an exhaustive and systematic sweep of all furniture and containers listed in the initial room observation to ensure no potential storage spot is overlooked.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Primary Furniture
description: Use this when common locations like desks or tables do not contain the required items.
---
Do not limit searches to the most obvious surface; if target items are not found, prioritize checking all other available storage units such as shelves, safes, and secondary tables rather than getting stuck re-checking the same few areas.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when the agent detects it is repeatedly visiting the same locations without progress.
---
Monitor the search history to identify and break out of search loops, and explicitly force the agent to traverse to unvisited locations to ensure the entire environment is covered.

---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

items.title: Target Specific Objects for Examination
items.description: Use this strategy when the task requires examining a specific item placed on a surface or within a container.
items.content: Do not settle for examining the surrounding furniture or surface where the item is located. Always perform the interaction action directly on the target object itself to ensure the system processes the request for the specific item rather than the container.

items.title: Sequencing Tool-Assisted Interactions
items.description: Use this strategy when a task implies that an object must be interacted with while a specific tool is active.
items.content: First, ensure the tool is in the necessary active state. Immediately following the tool's activation, execute the requested action directly on the target object, rather than interacting with the environment or the tool itself again.

items.title: Activating Appliances for State Changes
items.description: Use this when a task requires an object to attain a specific property, such as "hot" or "cooked."
items.content: Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance is insufficient to change its state. You must explicitly invoke the "turn on" or "operate" command to trigger the required transformation before retrieving the item for the next step.

items.title: Breaking Repetitive Action Loops
items.description: Use this when the agent finds itself repeatedly toggling the state (e.g., opening and closing) of a container without making progress.
items.content: If a cycle of opening and closing an appliance does not change the object's state or advance the task, stop the repetition immediately. Re-examine the available action space for an "activate" or "operate" command, or re-evaluate the next logical step in the task plan.

items.title: Prioritizing Final Placement After Modification
items.description: Use this when a multi-step task requires modifying an object and subsequently relocating it to a storage area.
items.content: After successfully modifying an object's state within an appliance, ensure you do not stop the task prematurely. Explicitly execute the action to pick up the modified object and move it to its final designated location to fulfill the objective.

judge.extraction_raw:
# Memory Item 1
## Title Activating Appliances for State Changes
## Description Use this when a task requires an object to attain a specific property, such as "hot" or "cooked."
## Content Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance is insufficient to change its state. You must explicitly invoke the "turn on" or "operate" command to trigger the required transformation before retrieving the item for the next step.

# Memory Item 2
## Title Breaking Repetitive Action Loops
## Description Use this when the agent finds itself repeatedly toggling the state (e.g., opening and closing) of a container without making progress.
## Content If a cycle of opening and closing an appliance does not change the object's state or advance the task, stop the repetition immediately. Re-examine the available action space for an "activate" or "operate" command, or re-evaluate the next logical step in the task plan.

# Memory Item 3
## Title Prioritizing Final Placement After Modification
## Description Use this when a multi-step task requires modifying an object and subsequently relocating it to a storage area.
## Content After successfully modifying an object's state within an appliance, ensure you do not stop the task prematurely. Explicitly execute the action to pick up the modified object and move it to its final designated location to fulfill the objective.

name: Action Sequence Planning

memory_context:
---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
---
Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

---
name: Systematic Search Expansion
description: Use this strategy when an initial search of nearby containers fails to yield the target object.
---
Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

---
name: Context-Aware Object Location
description: Use this strategy when searching for common household items that have specific state requirements (e.g., "clean").
---
If the object is not found in its typical storage location, broaden the search to include utility areas like sink basins or dish racks, as items may be located there waiting to be cleaned or dried. If the object is found in a dirty state, perform a cleaning action before proceeding with the rest of the task.

---
name: Object Search Strategy
description: Use this strategy when you cannot immediately locate a target object in its expected container.
---
If the object is not found in the primary storage appliance, systematically search other furniture and open surfaces such as countertops until the item is identified and can be picked up.

---
name: Workflow for State-Modifying Tasks
description: Use this sequence when a task requires an object to be in a specific state before being placed at a destination.
---
Always acquire the target object first, perform the necessary state-change operation (such as cooling or heating) using the appropriate appliance, and only then move the object to the final destination.

items.title: Systematic Searching in Storage Units
items.description: Use this strategy when the required object is not visible in the open environment.
items.content: Iteratively navigate to each available storage container (such as cabinets or drawers) and open them one by one to inspect their contents. Continue this process across all potential locations until the desired object is found.

items.title: Retrieving Objects from Closed Containers
items.description: Use this when a target object is detected or suspected to be inside a closed storage unit.
items.content: Before attempting to pick up an item, you must open the storage container to reveal its contents. Ensure the interaction sequence specifically includes an "open" action for the container before executing the "pick up" action for the object inside.

items.title: Transferring Items to a Destination Surface
items.description: Use this when the objective is to move a held item onto a specific furniture surface, such as a countertop or table.
items.content: Once the object is successfully held, navigate to the target destination surface. Execute the placement action to move the object from your inventory to the surface and confirm the transfer is complete.

If common household items (like plates or cups) are not found in cabinets or drawers, do not limit future searches to those same types of containers. Expand the search to include other logical locations such as dishwashers, open shelves, dining tables, or surfaces where items might have been left.

---
name: Maintain Search State to Avoid Redundant Loops
description: Use this strategy during long-running tasks involving repetitive searching of multiple containers.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected to prevent entering an infinite loop of re-visiting the same locations. If an exhaustive search of all accessible containers fails, stop repeating the search cycle and re-evaluate the environment to look for missed locations or alternative strategies.

---
name: Validate Object Availability via Scene Inspection
description: Use this strategy before initiating an exhaustive search for an object.
---
Carefully scan the initial room observation provided at the start of the task to determine if the target object exists in the environment. Do not blindly search containers if there is no indication that the object is present; prioritize identifying the object's presence or logical location based on the initial scene description.

---
name: Systematic Search Coverage
description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
---
Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

---
name: Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.
