memory_context:
---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

---
name: Container Interaction Workflow
description: Use whenever an object must be placed into or retrieved from a storage unit.
---
Always ensure the target container is open before attempting to move an object into or out of it. After completing the placement, remember to close the container to restore the scene's state and complete the task properly.

---
name: Activating Appliances for State Changes
description: Use this when a task requires an object to attain a specific property, such as "hot" or "cooked."
---
Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance is insufficient to change its state. You must explicitly invoke the "turn on" or "operate" command to trigger the required transformation before retrieving the item for the next step.

---
name: Breaking Repetitive Action Loops
description: Use this when the agent finds itself repeatedly toggling the state (e.g., opening and closing) of a container without making progress.
---
If a cycle of opening and closing an appliance does not change the object's state or advance the task, stop the repetition immediately. Re-examine the available action space for an "activate" or "operate" command, or re-evaluate the next logical step in the task plan.

items.content: Do not conclude the search phase after finding the first required object. Systematically traverse all reachable locations—such as countertops, cabinets, and basins—to locate the specified total quantity before attempting to place them.

items.title: Avoid Re-using Already Processed Objects
items.description: Use this strategy to prevent cycles of picking up and replacing the same item when the goal is to collect multiple objects.
items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit count of the items successfully placed in the target location. If the goal quantity is not met, do not re-interact with the objects you have already moved; instead, explore new locations to find different, distinct objects.

memory_context:
---
name: Parsing Spatial Constraints in Tasks
description: Use this strategy when a task instruction specifies a spatial relationship (e.g., "under", "next to", "inside") between two objects.
---
Do not assume that performing an action on the target object alone is sufficient. You must explicitly identify both the target object and the reference (landmark) object in the environment, then manipulate the target object to align with the specified spatial constraint relative to the reference object.

---
name: Verifying Environmental Preconditions
description: Use this strategy when an instruction requires examining an object under specific environmental conditions, such as a particular light source.
---
Do not merely execute an "examine" or "look" command on the target object if the task involves environmental factors. First, locate and activate the necessary utility (e.g., turning on a light source), then ensure the target object is positioned within the active field of that utility before performing the observation action.

---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

---
name: Systematic Exploration of the Environment
description: Use this strategy when the initial search for target objects fails to yield results.
---
Instead of repeatedly visiting the same locations, perform an exhaustive and systematic sweep of all furniture and containers listed in the initial room observation to ensure no potential storage spot is overlooked.

---
name: Systematic Search Coverage
description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
---
Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

---
name: Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.

---
name: Task Termination upon Search Exhaustion
description: Use this strategy when all potential locations in the environment have been checked for the target object.
---
If every accessible container and surface has been searched and the target object is still not found, conclude the task execution rather than continuing to move. Recognizing when an object is unavailable prevents the agent from entering an infinite loop of redundant actions.

---
name: Cooling Items
description: Use when the task requirement involves "cool [object]".
---
To cool an object, you must place it inside a fridge to change its state. Do not assume that randomly found objects are already at the required temperature; always locate and utilize a fridge to perform the cooling action before attempting to complete the task.

---
name: Action Sequence Planning
description: Use when a task requires multiple state changes (e.g., finding, then cooling, then placing).
---
Break complex tasks into distinct sub-goals: first retrieve the target object, then apply the necessary state transformations (like cooling in a fridge), and finally move the object to the destination. Do not attempt the final placement until the object satisfies all state constraints specified in the query.

---
name: Systematic Search Procedure
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Sequentially explore potential storage locations, such as cabinets, drawers, and open surfaces, by navigating to them and checking their contents until the target object is located.

---
name: Cooling Process
description: Use when an object needs to be cooled as part of a task.
---
Pick up the target object and interact with a cooling appliance while holding the object to apply the cooling effect; simply navigating to the cooling appliance is insufficient.

---
name: Post-Processing Placement
description: Use when an object needs to be moved to a destination surface after undergoing a transformation like cooling or heating.
---
Once the object has been processed, navigate to the target destination and execute the command to place the object there to finalize the task.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
---
Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

---
name: Systematic Search Expansion
description: Use this strategy when an initial search of nearby containers fails to yield the target object.
---
Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

---

memory_context:
---
name: Efficient Object Search Strategy
description: Use when the location of a target object is unknown within the current environment.
---
Begin by systematically checking containers and surface furniture. If the target object is not found in the initial set of locations, broaden the search to different types of furniture, such as switching from drawers to tabletops, until the item is discovered.

---
name: Object Retrieval and Placement Workflow
description: Use when tasked with moving a specific object to a designated destination.
---
Once the object is successfully located, pick it up and navigate directly to the target location. Place the object on the destination surface to complete the task, ensuring you verify the placement if the environment allows.

---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

items.title: Systematic Environment Exploration
items.description: Use when a task requires locating multiple instances of a specific object type within a room.
items.content: Instead of randomly traversing between locations, perform a systematic sweep of the room by grouping locations (e.g., surface areas first, then closed containers) to ensure complete coverage. Track visited locations to prevent redundant re-checking of empty furniture.

items.title: Search Priority Hierarchy
items.description: Use when searching for objects in environments with both open surfaces and closed containers.
items.content: Always prioritize inspecting open surfaces (tables, sofas, chairs) before expending actions to open drawers, cabinets, or other closed containers. Searching open surfaces is often faster and less resource-intensive, making it the most efficient first step to finding items.

items.title: Tracking Collection Progress
items.description: Use when the task requires collecting a specific number of objects (e.g., "put two boxes").
items.content: Actively track the count of collected objects versus the total required by the task. If a target quantity has not been reached, continue the search process until the entire environment has been exhausted or the requirement is fulfilled, rather than terminating the task prematurely.

items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit list of all containers (cabinets, drawers, fridges) that have already been fully inspected. Avoid repeatedly visiting the same locations and prioritize exploring unsearched containers to ensure the search is exhaustive and efficient.

items.title: Broadening Search Scope

items.content: If the target object is not present in primary locations such as the fridge or nearby cabinets, expand the search scope to include all available containers in the environment. items.title: Task Termination Policy

description: Use this process once the required object has been successfully located and acquired.
---

---
name: Systematic Surface Searching
description: When the target object is not immediately visible in the room, employ a methodical search pattern.
---

---
name: Object Retrieval and Placement

---

---

---

name: Retrieving Objects from Closed Storage
description: Use this when the required object is not visible in the current open environment.

---
name: Cleaning Objects using Water Sources
description: Use this when a task requires cleaning or washing an item.
---

---
name: Navigating to Target Locations
description: Use this when the task requires moving a processed object to a specific surface.
---
After completing necessary processing steps, identify the target destination. Navigate to that surface and place the object there to successfully finish the task.

---
name: Systematic Search Strategy
description: Use when attempting to locate a specific object within an environment containing many potential storage locations.
---
Instead of searching randomly or repeating checks on the same locations, proceed with a structured search pattern (e.g., scanning all storage units in a specific order, such as left-to-right or by proximity). This ensures that every container is checked once before assuming the object is missing.

---
name: Track Visited Locations
description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.
---
Maintain a mental or list-based log of containers that have already been opened and inspected. Avoid wasting time re-opening or re-visiting containers confirmed to be empty, and prioritize moving to unexplored areas to maximize search efficiency.

memory_context:
---
name: Cleaning Objects Prior to Storage
description: Use this strategy when the task requires an object to be in a "clean" state before it is placed in its final storage location.
---
Do not assume that an object retrieved from a countertop or table is already clean. Navigate to a sink or water source and perform the cleaning action on the object immediately before moving it to the target container.

---
name: Managing Enclosed Storage
description: Use this strategy when the destination for an object is a closed storage container such as a drawer or cabinet.
---
Always verify if the target container is open before attempting to place an object inside. If it is closed, perform an open action first, then proceed with the storage action, and finish by closing the container.

---
name: Systematic Search Strategy
description: Use when attempting to locate a specific object within an environment containing many potential storage locations.
---
Instead of searching randomly or repeating checks on the same locations, proceed with a structured search pattern (e.g., scanning all storage units in a specific order, such as left-to-right or by proximity). This ensures that every container is checked once before assuming the object is missing.

---
name: Track Visited Locations
description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.
---
Maintain a mental or list-based log of containers that have already been opened and inspected. Avoid wasting time re-opening or re-visiting containers confirmed to be empty, and prioritize moving to unexplored areas to maximize search efficiency.

---
name: Exhaustive Exploration
description: Use when primary locations (like the first few drawers or countertops) do not contain the target object.
---
Do not prematurely conclude the search if the target is not in the most obvious locations. Systematically expand the search scope to include all available furniture (such as all cabinets and drawers) until the object is found, rather than returning to previously checked areas.

description: Use when the required object for a task is not immediately available at the destination.
---

---

description: Use when a task requires moving an object from one location to another.
---

---

name: Systematic Search for Target Objects
description: Use this strategy when the requested object is not located in the initial high-probability storage containers.
---
Start by inspecting closed containers like drawers or cabinets where items are frequently stored. If the target is not found in these containers, expand the search to open surface areas such as tables or shelves, which are alternative locations for small items.

---
name: Selecting from Multiple Candidates
description: Use this strategy when your scan identifies multiple instances of the requested object.
---
If the environment contains multiple units of the required item, any single instance is sufficient to complete the task. Select the most accessible unit to minimize movement and reduce the number of actions required.

---
name: Systematic Exploration Strategy
description: Use this strategy when searching for an object that is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Instead of repeatedly checking a small subset of locations, generate a checklist of all potential receptacles (e.g., tables, cabinets, drawers, surfaces) identified in the initial room observation and visit each one methodically until the target object is located.

---
name: Prevent Repetitive Search Cycles
description: Use this when navigating a room to find an object to avoid getting stuck in infinite loops.
---
Maintain a record of locations already searched; if you find yourself visiting the same sequence of furniture multiple times without success, force a change in strategy and pivot to exploring previously unvisited areas of the room.

---
name: Broaden Search Scope to All Surfaces
description: Use this when you cannot locate a specific item in expected storage containers.
---
If the target object is not found in primary storage locations like drawers or cabinets, expand the search to all available surfaces mentioned in the scene, such as tables, chairs, beds, or floors. Do not ignore non-storage furniture simply because it seems like an unlikely place to hold the item.

name: Broaden Search Scope for Missing Items
description: Use when initial checks of common storage locations like cabinets fail to reveal the target object.
---
If standard storage containers are empty, systematically expand your search to include alternative locations such as drawers, dishwashers, sinks, or directly on furniture surfaces like countertops and dining tables. Do not limit exploration only to the first few categories of containers encountered.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Loops
description: Use when you are unable to find an object after completing an initial sweep of the environment.
---
Implement a tracking mechanism to ensure you do not repeatedly check the same locations, as this indicates a failure to find the object in the current area. If a full sweep yields no results, stop searching those locations and conclude that the object is not present in the current area rather than cycling through the same containers.

---
name: Prioritize Visible Objects Before Opening Containers
description: Use at the beginning of a retrieval task to minimize unnecessary actions.
---
Before systematically opening closed containers, perform an exhaustive scan of all visible surfaces in the room to see if the target item is already sitting in plain sight. Often, objects are left on countertops, tables, or near sinks, rendering the effort of opening multiple cabinets unnecessary.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Storage
description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in standard storage containers like drawers or cabinets.
---
If initial searches in drawers and cabinets prove unsuccessful, broaden your search to include countertops, sinks, appliances, and tables, as kitchen tools are often left on functional surfaces rather than being put away.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty containers.
---
Maintain a mental record of previously searched locations and avoid revisiting them; if a search area is exhausted, systematically move to new, unsearched containers or furniture types to maximize search efficiency.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search Procedure
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Sequentially explore potential storage locations, such as cabinets, drawers, and open surfaces, by navigating to them and checking their contents until the target object is located.

---
name: Cooling Process
description: Use when an object needs to be cooled as part of a task.
---
Pick up the target object and interact with a cooling appliance while holding the object to apply the cooling effect; simply navigating to the cooling appliance is insufficient.

---
name: Post-Processing Placement
description: Use when an object needs to be moved to a destination surface after undergoing a transformation like cooling or heating.
---
Once the object has been processed, navigate to the target destination and execute the command to place the object there to finalize the task.

---
name: Activating Appliances for Heating
description: Use this when a task requires heating an object inside an appliance.
---
Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance does not automatically start the process. You must perform a specific action to activate the device (e.g., "turn on" or "operate") to initiate the heating of the object.

---
name: Validating Heating Completion
description: Use this after attempting to heat an object to confirm the task is finished before removing the item.
---
Before removing an object from a heating appliance, verify that the object's state has changed to "heated." Repeatedly opening and closing the appliance does not trigger the heating process; ensure an explicit activation action is performed first.

memory_context:
---
name: Activating Appliances for State Changes
description: Use this when a task requires an object to attain a specific property, such as "hot" or "cooked."
---
Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance is insufficient to change its state. You must explicitly invoke the "turn on" or "operate" command to trigger the required transformation before retrieving the item for the next step.

---
name: Breaking Repetitive Action Loops
description: Use this when the agent finds itself repeatedly toggling the state (e.g., opening and closing) of a container without making progress.
---
If a cycle of opening and closing an appliance does not change the object's state or advance the task, stop the repetition immediately. Re-examine the available action space for an "activate" or "operate" command, or re-evaluate the next logical step in the task plan.

---
name: Prioritizing Final Placement After Modification
description: Use this when a multi-step task requires modifying an object and subsequently relocating it to a storage area.
---
After successfully modifying an object's state within an appliance, ensure you do not stop the task prematurely. Explicitly execute the action to pick up the modified object and move it to its final designated location to fulfill the objective.

---
name: Systematic Search for Missing Objects
description: Use this procedure when the required target object is not immediately visible in the current location.
---
Iteratively navigate to all nearby potential storage containers, such as cabinets and drawers, and open them one by one to inspect their contents until the object is found.

---
name: Modifying Object State via Appliances
description: Use this strategy when an object must be at a specific temperature (e.g., heated or cooled) before completing the task.
---
After obtaining the object, locate an appliance capable of changing its state, such as a cooling or heating device. Interact with the appliance using the object to achieve the required state before proceeding to the target destination.

items.title: Recognizing Goal Completion
items.description: Use this item when the agent has successfully placed an object into a target container.
items.content: Once the object is placed in the desired destination, stop all further interaction with that object. Do not attempt to re-examine or manipulate the object after successful placement, as the task is considered complete at that point.

items.title: Avoid Unnecessary Object Extraction
items.description: Use this item when the agent reaches a target receptacle with an item already placed inside.
items.content: Do not pick up or remove an object from its target container once it has been successfully deposited. If verification is necessary, use passive observation commands rather than physical interaction to check the status of the container.

items.title: Streamlining Device Interaction
items.description: Use this item when interacting with appliances or containers that require multiple steps to operate (e.g., heating or closing).
items.content: Execute interaction sequences linearly (e.g., open, insert, close, activate) and avoid redundant cycles of opening and closing. Repetitive or cyclic interactions often lead to accidental state reversals, such as removing an object that was just successfully placed.

memory_context:
---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Loops
description: When a search for a target object has failed in specific locations.
---
If you have inspected a set of containers or surfaces and found the target object absent, immediately mark these locations as exhausted and prioritize searching new, unexplored areas. Do not allow the agent to fall into a repetitive cycle of revisiting the same locations, as this wastes steps and prevents task completion.

---
name: Systematic Exploration Strategy
description: When the target object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Formulate a systematic search path that covers all potential storage containers (such as all cabinets or drawers) in the environment rather than randomly selecting or oscillating between a small subset. If an initial search fails, consciously expand the search radius to include the next set of unexplored containers to ensure the entire room is covered.

---
name: Prioritizing Logical Storage Locations
description: When searching for kitchenware or cooking equipment.
---
Instead of inspecting surfaces or random containers, prioritize high-probability locations such as cabinets and drawers when looking for movable objects like cookware. Use the initial room observation to inventory all available storage units and plan a sequence to visit them, rather than relying on trial and error.

---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search Strategy
description: Use when attempting to locate a specific object within an environment containing many potential storage locations.
---
Instead of searching randomly or repeating checks on the same locations, proceed with a structured search pattern (e.g., scanning all storage units in a specific order, such as left-to-right or by proximity). This ensures that every container is checked once before assuming the object is missing.

---
name: Track Visited Locations
description: Use when an object is not found in the initial inspection of containers.
---
Maintain a mental or list-based log of containers that have already been opened and inspected. Avoid wasting time re-opening or re-visiting containers confirmed to be empty, and prioritize moving to unexplored areas to maximize search efficiency.

---
name: Exhaustive Exploration
description: Use when primary locations (like the first few drawers or countertops) do not contain the target object.
---
Do not prematurely conclude the search if the target is not in the most obvious locations. Systematically expand the search scope to include all available furniture (such as all cabinets and drawers) until the object is found, rather than returning to previously checked areas.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this strategy when the agent finds itself repeatedly checking the same set of containers during a search.
---
Maintain a checklist of all containers already inspected during the task. Immediately exclude containers that have been confirmed empty from future navigation to ensure the agent focuses exploration on unvisited locations rather than looping through the same area.

---
name: Systematic Search Expansion
description: Use this strategy when an initial search of nearby containers fails to yield the target object.
---
Instead of fixating on a small cluster of furniture, systematically iterate through all available storage containers in the environment. Prioritize a breadth-first search across all cabinets, drawers, and surfaces in the room to maximize the probability of finding the object.

name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the location of a target object is unknown and needs to be discovered within a room.
---
Iteratively navigate to various potential storage surfaces or containers, such as shelves, basins, or counters, and inspect the immediate vicinity until the target object is successfully identified.

---
name: Surface Inspection
description: Use this when you have arrived at a location but cannot immediately identify the target object among the visible items.
---
Perform an explicit examination action on the container or surface to reveal any items that might be obscured or missed in the initial arrival observation.

---
name: Object Relocation Procedure
description: Use this workflow when the task requires transferring an object to a specific destination.
---
After successfully acquiring the target object, navigate directly to the destination container and execute the placement action to complete the transfer.

---
name: Cleaning before Storage
description: Use when the task explicitly requires an item to be in a specific condition, such as "clean," before it is placed in its final location.
---
Before moving an object to its storage destination, verify if it needs to be cleaned and perform the cleaning action at a sink or basin. This prevents the need to retrieve the item from storage later to fulfill the condition.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Objects
description: Use when the target object is not immediately visible in the starting location.
---
Systematically visit potential storage areas, including basins, countertops, and cabinets. If the object is not on a surface, interact with closed containers by opening them to inspect their contents until the target is found.

---
name: Recursive Object Searching
description: Use this strategy when the target items are not found on open surfaces or within primary storage locations like drawers.
---
If an initial scan of furniture surfaces and drawers fails to reveal the target, inspect the contents of containers (such as boxes, baskets, or cases) found on those surfaces, as they often contain hidden items.

---
name: Comprehensive Environmental Scanning
description: Use this when searching for items that are frequently misplaced on furniture rather than stored in containers.
---
Expand the search scope to include all furniture surfaces, such as beds, chairs, and tables, as items are often placed on top of these objects rather than exclusively inside designated storage units.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when an initial sweep of a room's storage locations fails to locate the target objects.
---
Maintain a log of inspected areas to prevent repeating visits to the exact same containers, and instead pivot to checking entirely new locations or categories of furniture if the current search strategy proves unproductive.

---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Exploration Strategy
description: Use this strategy when searching for an object that is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Instead of repeatedly checking a small subset of locations, generate a checklist of all potential receptacles (e.g., tables, cabinets, drawers, surfaces) identified in the initial room observation and visit each one methodically until the target object is located.

---
name: Prevent Repetitive Search Cycles
description: Use this when navigating a room to find an object to avoid getting stuck in infinite loops.
---
Maintain a record of locations already searched; if you find yourself visiting the same sequence of furniture multiple times without success, force a change in strategy and pivot to exploring previously unvisited areas of the room.

---
name: Broaden Search Scope to All Surfaces
description: Use this when you cannot locate a specific item in expected storage containers.
---
If the target object is not found in primary storage locations like drawers or cabinets, expand the search to all available surfaces mentioned in the scene, such as tables, chairs, beds, or floors. Do not ignore non-storage furniture simply because it seems like an unlikely place to hold the item.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not immediately visible in the environment.
---
Prioritize searching inside closed containers like drawers or cabinets first. If the target object is not found in these storage areas, systematically shift the search to open surface areas, such as countertops or tables, where objects are frequently left exposed.

---
name: Target-Oriented Object Relocation
description: Use this process once the required object has been successfully located and acquired.
---
After picking up the required object, navigate directly to the designated destination location. Complete the task by performing a placement action to move the held object onto or into the target receptacle or surface.

---
name: Searching for items based on spatial descriptions
description: Use this when a task specifies a relative position (e.g., "under" or "next to" a reference object) for a target item.
---
If the target item is not visible on the immediate surface of the reference object, do not just re-examine the same surface; inspect the supporting furniture for hidden compartments (like drawers) or check the area directly beneath the furniture unit itself to locate the item.

---
name: Avoiding action repetition
description: Use this when the agent finds itself performing identical sequences of observations without success.
---
If repeated `examine` or `look` actions at a specific location consistently fail to reveal the target, stop executing redundant actions at that site. Instead, broaden the search scope to check other relevant containers or furniture in the vicinity to prevent getting stuck in a loop.

---
name: Parsing Spatial Constraints in Tasks
description: Use this strategy when a task instruction specifies a spatial relationship (e.g., "under", "next to", "inside") between two objects.
---
Do not assume that performing an action on the target object alone is sufficient. You must explicitly identify both the target object and the reference (landmark) object in the environment, then manipulate the target object to align with the specified spatial constraint relative to the reference object.

---
name: Verifying Environmental Preconditions
description: Use this strategy when an instruction requires examining an object under specific environmental conditions, such as a particular light source.
---
Do not merely execute an "examine" or "look" command on the target object if the task involves environmental factors. First, locate and activate the necessary utility (e.g., turning on a light source), then ensure the target object is positioned within the active field of that utility before performing the observation action.

---
name: Broadening Search Scope
description: When a target object is not found on or near the primary location, do not restrict the search to those areas.
---
If an initial search of primary surfaces and containers yields no results, systematically inspect all other furniture and containers in the room, such as dressers or beds, before concluding the object is missing or re-checking previous locations.

---
name: Recursive Object Searching
description: Use this strategy when the target items are not found on open surfaces or within primary storage locations like drawers.
---
If an initial scan of furniture surfaces and drawers fails to reveal the target, inspect the contents of containers (such as boxes, baskets, or cases) found on those surfaces, as they often contain hidden items.

---
name: Comprehensive Environmental Scanning
description: Use this when searching for items that are frequently misplaced on furniture rather than stored in containers.
---
Expand the search scope to include all furniture surfaces, such as beds, chairs, and tables, as items are often placed on top of these objects rather than exclusively inside designated storage units.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when an initial sweep of a room's storage locations fails to locate the target objects.
---
Maintain a log of inspected areas to prevent repeating visits to the exact same containers, and instead pivot to checking entirely new locations or categories of furniture if the current search strategy proves unproductive.

---
name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search Coverage
description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
---
Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

---
name: Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.

---
name: Task Termination upon Search Exhaustion
description: Use this strategy when all potential locations in the environment have been checked for the target object.
---
If every accessible container and surface has been searched and the target object is still not found, conclude the task execution rather than continuing to move. Recognizing when an object is unavailable prevents the agent from entering an infinite loop of redundant actions.

---
name: Activating Appliances for Heating
description: Use this when a task requires heating an object inside an appliance.
---
Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance does not automatically start the process. You must perform a specific action to activate the device (e.g., "turn on" or "operate") to initiate the heating of the object.

---
name: Validating Heating Completion
description: Use this after attempting to heat an object to confirm the task is finished before removing the item.
---
Before removing an object from a heating appliance, verify that the object's state has changed to "heated." Repeatedly opening and closing the appliance does not trigger the heating process; ensure an explicit activation action is performed first.

name: Verifying Environmental Preconditions

---

---

Do not blindly search containers if there is no indication that the object is present; prioritize identifying the object's presence or logical location based on the initial scene description.

---
name: Systematic Search Coverage
description: Use this strategy when the target object is not found in the most obvious location (e.g., the fridge).
---
Maintain a mental or explicit checklist of all containers and surfaces in the environment. Systematically visit every unexplored location one by one to ensure full coverage, rather than focusing exclusively on a small subset of locations or randomly switching between them.

---
name: Preventing Repetitive Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to prevent the agent from repeatedly checking the same empty locations.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected. Once a container has been verified as empty, mark it as "exhausted" and exclude it from future search iterations to avoid circular navigation.

memory_context:
---
name: Target Specific Objects for Examination
description: Use this strategy when the task requires examining a specific item placed on a surface or within a container.
---
Do not settle for examining the surrounding furniture or surface where the item is located. Always perform the interaction action directly on the target object itself to ensure the system processes the request for the specific item rather than the container.

---
name: Sequencing Tool-Assisted Interactions
description: Use this strategy when a task implies that an object must be interacted with while a specific tool is active.
---
First, ensure the tool is in the necessary active state. Immediately following the tool's activation, execute the requested action directly on the target object, rather than interacting with the environment or the tool itself again.

---
name: Systematic Exploration of the Environment
description: Use this strategy when the initial search for target objects fails to yield results.
---
Instead of repeatedly visiting the same locations, perform an exhaustive and systematic sweep of all furniture and containers listed in the initial room observation to ensure no potential storage spot is overlooked.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Primary Furniture
description: Use this when common locations like desks or tables do not contain the required items.
---
Do not limit searches to the most obvious surface; if target items are not found, prioritize checking all other available storage units such as shelves, safes, and secondary tables rather than getting stuck re-checking the same few areas.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when the agent detects it is repeatedly visiting the same locations without progress.
---
Monitor the search history to identify and break out of search loops, and explicitly force the agent to traverse to unvisited locations to ensure the entire environment is covered.

items.title: Spatial Proximity for Dependent Tasks
items.description: Use when a task requires using an external tool (e.g., a lamp) to examine or manipulate another object.
items.content: Ensure both the target object and the required tool are located in the same spatial vicinity or held simultaneously before performing the final interaction, as activating a tool in a remote location will not affect the target object.

items.title: Re-verifying Conditions After State Changes
items.description: Use when a task requires an object to be in a specific environment or state for a successful outcome.
items.content: If you modify the environment (such as activating a light source), do not assume the previous examination or manipulation is sufficient; perform the target action again to observe the object under the new conditions.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Exploration of the Environment
description: Use this strategy when the initial search for target objects fails to yield results.
---
Instead of repeatedly visiting the same locations, perform an exhaustive and systematic sweep of all furniture and containers listed in the initial room observation to ensure no potential storage spot is overlooked.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Primary Furniture
description: Use this when common locations like desks or tables do not contain the required items.
---
Do not limit searches to the most obvious surface; if target items are not found, prioritize checking all other available storage units such as shelves, safes, and secondary tables rather than getting stuck re-checking the same few areas.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when the agent detects it is repeatedly visiting the same locations without progress.
---
Monitor the search history to identify and break out of search loops, and explicitly force the agent to traverse to unvisited locations to ensure the entire environment is covered.

---
name: Target Specific Objects for Examination
description: Use this strategy when the task requires examining a specific item placed on a surface or within a container.
---
Do not settle for examining the surrounding furniture or surface where the item is located. Always perform the interaction action directly on the target object itself to ensure the system processes the request for the specific item rather than the container.

---
name: Sequencing Tool-Assisted Interactions
description: Use this strategy when a task implies that an object must be interacted with while a specific tool is active.
---
First, ensure the tool is in the necessary active state. Immediately following the tool's activation, execute the requested action directly on the target object, rather than interacting with the environment or the tool itself again.

---

---
name: Conducting Systematic Searches
description: Use when a target object is not immediately found in the most likely locations.
---
Do not rely on checking the same few containers repeatedly. Maintain a mental checklist of unexamined containers and visit them sequentially, ensuring all relevant storage units (cabinets, drawers, appliances) are checked before assuming the object is not present in the environment.

---
name: Preventing Repetitive Search Cycles
description: Use when the agent tends to oscillate between a small subset of locations.
---
Monitor the sequence of locations visited to avoid getting stuck in a loop. If a pattern of repetition is identified, prioritize moving to an unvisited location or a different type of container to break the cycle and force the search to expand to new areas.

---
name: Cooling an Object
description: Use when a task requires an object to be cooled.
---

memory_context:
---
name: Broaden Search Scope for Missing Items
description: Use when initial checks of common storage locations like cabinets fail to reveal the target object.
---
If standard storage containers are empty, systematically expand your search to include alternative locations such as drawers, dishwashers, sinks, or directly on furniture surfaces like countertops and dining tables. Do not limit exploration only to the first few categories of containers encountered.

---
name: Avoid Redundant Search Loops
description: Use when you are unable to find an object after completing an initial sweep of the environment.
---
Implement a tracking mechanism to ensure you do not repeatedly check the same locations, as this indicates a failure to find the object in the current area. If a full sweep yields no results, stop searching those locations and conclude that the object is not present in the current area rather than cycling through the same containers.

---
name: Prioritize Visible Objects Before Opening Containers
description: Use at the beginning of a retrieval task to minimize unnecessary actions.
---
Before systematically opening closed containers, perform an exhaustive scan of all visible surfaces in the room to see if the target item is already sitting in plain sight. Often, objects are left on countertops, tables, or near sinks, rendering the effort of opening multiple cabinets unnecessary.

---
name: Systematic Search Coverage
description: Use this when the target object is not immediately visible in the environment to avoid leaving potential storage locations unexamined.
---
Maintain an internal state of visited versus unvisited containers to ensure a systematic sweep of the room. Avoid revisiting locations that have already been confirmed as empty, ensuring efficient coverage of all potential storage spaces without repeating actions.

---
name: Semantic Prioritization
description: Use this to decide which containers to check first when searching for a specific type of object.
---
Leverage common-sense associations between object categories and locations (e.g., cooking utensils are typically found in drawers or cabinets near food preparation areas). Prioritize searching these high-probability areas before resorting to a blind or uniform search of all furniture in the room.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Search Management
description: Use when an object is not found in the initial locations checked to avoid redundant, infinite search loops.
---
Instead of repeatedly checking the same few locations, maintain a mental or explicit list of visited containers. If the search reaches a point where the object has not been located, systematically expand the search to unvisited areas like drawers, countertops, or other appliances.

---
name: Task Pre-Condition Analysis
description: Use when a task involves a transformation step (such as cooling or heating) before the final placement.
---
Break down the request into sequential sub-tasks: locate the target, perform the required transformation (e.g., placing the item in the appropriate appliance to cool/heat), and then execute the final placement. Ensure that intermediate transformation steps are not skipped or ignored during the planning phase.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope
description: Use when standard storage containers like cabinets have been exhausted without finding the target object.
---
Do not limit the search strictly to cabinets; immediately pivot to checking countertops, drawers, refrigerators, and other visible surfaces in the environment. Broaden the search criteria early to include all potential holding areas described in the initial scene observation.

---
name: Systematic Exhaustive Search
description: Use this strategy when the initial inspection of common areas fails to locate the target object.
---
Do not rely on visiting a small subset of locations repeatedly. Instead, implement a systematic search plan that involves visiting and inspecting every available storage container (such as all cabinets, drawers, and fridges) sequentially to ensure the entire environment is covered before concluding the object is missing.

---
name: Redundant Visit Avoidance
description: Use this strategy to prevent wasting moves by returning to locations previously confirmed to be empty.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit list of containers that have been visited and verified as empty. Avoid navigating to these locations again, as it creates an inefficient loop that delays the discovery of the target object in unsearched areas.

description: Use this strategy when a task instruction specifies a spatial relationship (e.g., "under", "next to", "inside") between two objects.
---

You must explicitly identify both the target object and the reference (landmark) object in the environment, then manipulate the target object to align with the specified spatial constraint relative to the reference object.

description: Use this strategy when an instruction requires examining an object under specific environmental conditions, such as a particular light source.
---

name: Fulfilling State-Based Requirements
description: When a task specifies a target state for an object (e.g., "hot"), treat this as a transformation step rather than a search for a pre-existing object.
---

name: Operating Heating Appliances
description: Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance is insufficient to achieve a "hot" state.
---

---
name: Task Sequencing and Loop Avoidance
description: Avoid repetitive, unproductive actions, such as repeatedly opening and closing an appliance door without attempting to activate the device or complete the next stage of the task.
---
If the current interaction sequence is not changing the object's state or moving it toward the final destination, stop the current cycle and re-evaluate the plan to identify the missing step, such as turning on a machine or moving to a different container.

name: Broaden Search Locations for Common Objects
description: Use this strategy when a required object is not found in the primary set of containers initially searched.
---
If common household items (like plates or cups) are not found in cabinets or drawers, do not limit future searches to those same types of containers. Expand the search to include other logical locations such as dishwashers, open shelves, dining tables, or surfaces where items might have been left.

---
name: Maintain Search State to Avoid Redundant Loops
description: Use this strategy during long-running tasks involving repetitive searching of multiple containers.
---
Keep track of which containers have already been opened and inspected to prevent entering an infinite loop of re-visiting the same locations. If an exhaustive search of all accessible containers fails, stop repeating the search cycle and re-evaluate the environment to look for missed locations or alternative strategies.

items.title: Systematic Location Tracking
items.description: Use this strategy when searching for a specific item across multiple containers in an environment.
items.content: Maintain a mental or explicit list of all containers (cabinets, drawers, fridges) that have already been searched. Once a container has been inspected and confirmed empty, do not visit it again, focusing instead on unexamined locations to maximize search efficiency.

items.title: Exhaustive Search Strategy
items.description: Use this when a target object is not found in the most obvious or primary location (e.g., the fridge for food).
items.content: If the primary storage location is empty, immediately pivot to a systematic search of all other reachable storage units, such as cabinets, drawers, and pantries, regardless of whether they are traditionally associated with the target item. Do not abandon the task until all potential storage containers in the environment have been opened and examined.

items.title: Identifying and Breaking Search Loops
items.description: Use this to prevent the agent from getting stuck in a cycle of visiting the same few locations repeatedly.
items.content: If the agent observes that it is visiting the same set of locations multiple times without success, force a change in the navigation path by explicitly selecting a new, unvisited container. If a cycle of repetitive actions continues, it indicates that the current search strategy is exhausted, and the agent should conclude the task rather than looping indefinitely.

name: Prioritizing State Changes
description: Use this when a task requires an object to undergo a state change (e.g., cooling) before final placement.
---
Ensure the object undergoes the required state-changing action using the appropriate appliance before transferring it to the final destination. This prevents unnecessary backtracking and re-handling of the object if it was moved to the target location prematurely.

---
name: Sequential Object Searching
description: Use this when the required object is not immediately visible in the initial storage area.
---
If an object is not found in its typical storage location, systematically search adjacent surfaces and alternative containers. Maintain awareness of the search area and expand the range of visited locations until the target object is located.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this procedure when the target object is not immediately visible in the current location.
---
Iteratively navigate to available open surfaces, such as countertops or tables, to locate the target item; if the item is not found, extend the search to enclosed storage containers.

---
name: Processing Objects Before Final Placement
description: Use this procedure when a task requires an object to have a specific state (e.g., temperature) before reaching its final destination.
---
After acquiring the object, locate and utilize an appropriate appliance to perform the necessary state change—such as heating or cooling—before proceeding to the final drop-off location.

---
name: Activating Appliances for Heating
description: Use this when a task requires heating an object inside an appliance.
---
Simply placing an object inside a heating appliance does not automatically start the process. You must perform a specific action to activate the device (e.g., "turn on" or "operate") to initiate the heating of the object.

items.title: Systematic Search of Receptacles
items.description: Use this when searching for an object in a new environment to ensure all potential storage locations are inspected.
items.content: Maintain a list of all available receptacles (e.g., shelves, basins, drawers, garbage cans) present in the environment and visit each one sequentially. Mark containers as "searched" or simply avoid visiting the same set of locations repeatedly, ensuring a breadth-first search across all possible storage areas.

items.title: Expanding Search Scope
items.description: Use this when an initial, limited search of common furniture fails to yield the target object.
items.content: Do not restrict search behavior to only primary storage locations like shelves or tables; include less conventional containers such as garbage cans, wall-mounted holders, or toilet areas. Systematically inspect every unique receptacle mentioned in the initial environment observation before concluding the search.

items.title: Identifying Exhaustive Search Failure
items.description: Use this to prevent infinite loops when an object is not present in the environment.
items.content: If you have inspected every accessible container in the scene without locating the target object, stop the task execution. Avoiding repetitive cycles once the search space is fully exhausted is crucial to preventing performance degradation and indicating that the object cannot be retrieved.

name: Systematic Searching in Storage Units
description: Use this strategy when the required object is not visible in the open environment.
---
Iteratively navigate to each available storage container (such as cabinets or drawers) and open them one by one to inspect their contents. Continue this process across all potential locations until the desired object is found.

---
name: Retrieving Objects from Closed Containers
description: Use this when a target object is detected or suspected to be inside a closed storage unit.
---
Before attempting to pick up an item, you must open the storage container to reveal its contents. Ensure the interaction sequence specifically includes an "open" action for the container before executing the "pick up" action for the object inside.

---
name: Transferring Items to a Destination Surface
description: Use this when the objective is to move a held item onto a specific furniture surface, such as a countertop or table.
---
Once the object is successfully held, navigate to the target destination surface. Execute the placement action to move the object from your inventory to the surface and confirm the transfer is complete.

---
name: Comprehensive Search for Multiple Instances
description: Use this strategy when the task requires collecting or interacting with multiple instances of the same object type.
---
Do not conclude the search phase after finding the first required object. Systematically traverse all reachable locations—such as countertops, cabinets, and basins—to locate the specified total quantity before attempting to place them.

---
name: Avoid Re-using Already Processed Objects
description: Use this strategy to prevent cycles of picking up and replacing the same item when the goal is to collect multiple objects.
---
Maintain a mental or explicit count of the items successfully placed in the target location. If the goal quantity is not met, do not re-interact with the objects you have already moved; instead, explore new locations to find different, distinct objects.

---
name: Managing Multi-Item Collection Tasks
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same type of object to a destination.
---
Implement a "retrieve and place" loop: travel to the source location, pick up one instance of the target object, travel to the destination, and place the object. Repeat these steps sequentially until the required number of items has been successfully transferred to the target.

---
name: Maintaining Awareness of Inventory and Progress
description: Use this whenever you are unsure about the quantity of objects collected or need to confirm which items are ready to be transported.
---
Before moving to a destination, use inventory checks to verify current holdings. Utilize examination actions on source containers to confirm whether additional target objects remain to be picked up, ensuring no items are missed during the collection process.

---
name: Systematic Object Search
description: Use this when the location of the target object is unknown at the start of the task.
---
Sequentially navigate to and inspect potential support surfaces—such as tables, shelves, or counters—until the target object is identified, avoiding the assumption that the item is in a specific pre-determined location.

---
name: Container Access Verification
description: Use this when the destination for an object is a closable container, such as a drawer or cabinet.
---
Upon arriving at the target container, always verify its current state and open it if it is closed before attempting to deposit the object, ensuring the destination is accessible for the interaction.

---
name: Systematic Object Location Search
description: Use when you need to find an object but do not know its current location.
---
Systematically navigate to and inspect surfaces like tables, stands, and counters to locate the target item before attempting to interact with it.

items.title: Ensuring Container Accessibility
items.description: Use this when the target destination for an item is a closed storage unit.
items.content: Before attempting to place an item inside a storage unit, verify that the container is open; if it is closed, you must perform an opening action before depositing the object.

items.title: Handling Tasks Involving Multiple Items
items.description: Use this when a task requires collecting and moving multiple instances of the same object type.
items.content: Instead of attempting to gather all items simultaneously, iterate through the process of picking up a single item, traveling to the destination, and depositing it before returning to the source to collect the next item.

items.title: Locating Items in Clustered Environments

items.content: If you successfully locate one instance of the required object type, inspect the immediate vicinity of that location, as multiple instances are frequently grouped together in the same storage area.

name: Heating or Cooling Objects
description: Use this when a task requires an object to have a specific state (e.g., "hot," "chilled") before being placed in its final location.
---

---
name: Sequential Goal Execution
description: Use this when a task involves both transforming an object and moving it to a destination.
---
Break the task into logical phases: acquire the object, perform the transformation (heating/cooling), and finally transport it to the goal location. Ensure the ultimate destination is not ignored after the transformation step is complete.

---
name: Loop Detection and Reassessment
description: Use this when you find yourself repeatedly executing the same actions (e.g., opening and closing a door) without observing a change in the object's properties or the task's status.
---
If repetition does not progress the task, stop and re-evaluate the sequence; you are likely missing a required step, such as turning on an appliance, or using the wrong appliance for the intended transformation.

---
name: Systematic Search Strategy for Target Objects
description: When an object is not immediately visible in the environment and must be retrieved.
---
Before initiating navigation, scan the environment to identify potential locations. Maintain a record of locations visited and prioritize searching storage containers (like cabinets, drawers, or appliances) systematically rather than moving randomly between them.

---
name: Task Decomposition for Object State Modifications
description: When the task requires an object to have a specific property (e.g., temperature or state).
---
Recognize that the task may require a multi-stage process: locating the object, performing a transformation (such as heating or preparing), and then executing the final placement. Before moving to the destination, check if the retrieved object satisfies the required condition; if not, identify and use the appropriate tool or appliance to modify it.

name: Systematic Search of All Potential Containers
description: Use this strategy when target objects are not visible on surfaces or in primary search areas.
---
Instead of limiting the search to specific furniture types like shelves or drawers, conduct an exhaustive sweep of all interactable containers in the room, including beds, sidetables, and garbage cans. If an object is not found, ensure that every accessible storage unit has been opened and examined before concluding the search.

---
name: Prevent Infinite Search Loops
description: Use this strategy to ensure the agent stops searching when all potential locations have been exhausted.
---
Maintain a mental record or checklist of locations that have already been searched and confirmed empty. Avoid re-visiting or re-examining the same furniture repeatedly; if a complete sweep of the environment has been performed without locating the target, terminate the search process rather than oscillating between empty locations.

---
name: Prioritize High-Density Locations
description: When a task requires gathering multiple instances of the same object, use this strategy to minimize navigation.
---
If you encounter a location that contains multiple instances of the required target object, exhaust that location by collecting them one by one before searching elsewhere. This prevents unnecessary travel between different containers or surfaces.

---
name: Iterative Transport Strategy
description: Use this workflow when you must move multiple items to a single destination.
---
Instead of attempting to gather all items before moving, establish a repetitive loop: navigate to the source, pick up one instance of the object, move to the destination to deposit it, and return to the source. Repeat this sequence until the total required quantity is successfully transported.

---
name: Systematic Container Search
description: Use this strategy to avoid wasting moves by re-checking containers that have already been explored.
---
Track which containers you have already opened and inspected. If a container has been checked and found empty, mark it as searched and do not revisit it unless there is a specific reason to believe the object state has changed.

items.content: To simplify inventory management, transport objects one by one rather than attempting to carry multiple items simultaneously. Successfully place the first item into the storage container before returning to the source location to retrieve the remaining items.

items.title: Preparing Storage Containers
items.description: Use this whenever you need to place items into a closed storage unit such as a drawer or cabinet.
items.content: Always verify the state of the storage container upon arrival. If the container is closed, perform the appropriate action to open it before attempting to deposit your carried item inside.

judge.extraction_raw:
# Memory Item 1
## Title Searching for Clustered Objects
## Description Use this when the task requires locating multiple instances of a specific type of item within a room.
## Content Prioritize searching on flat surfaces like dining tables or countertops, as multiple related items are often stored together in these areas. If the initial location does not contain enough items, systematically check other similar surfaces in the environment until the target quantity is found.

# Memory Item 2
## Title Sequential Transport Strategy
## Description Use this when gathering and moving multiple items to a single storage destination.
## Content To simplify inventory management, transport objects one by one rather than attempting to carry multiple items simultaneously. Successfully place the first item into the storage container before returning to the source location to retrieve the remaining items.

# Memory Item 3
## Title Preparing Storage Containers
## Description Use this whenever you need to place items into a closed storage unit such as a drawer or cabinet.
## Content Always verify the state of the storage container upon arrival. If the container is closed, perform the appropriate action to open it before attempting to deposit your carried item inside.

memory_context:
---
name: Sequential Handling of Multiple Items
description: Use this strategy when the task requires moving multiple instances of the same object type to a single destination.
---
Perform the pickup and placement actions for each individual item in a complete cycle (pick up, move, deposit) until the total required count of items has been successfully transferred to the target location.

---
name: Locating Target Objects in Bulk
description: Use this strategy when you need to collect multiple items to fulfill a placement task.
---
Before starting, scan the environment for surfaces or containers that hold multiple instances of the required object type; navigating to a location containing multiple targets minimizes the number of travel actions needed to gather all items.

---
name: Systematic Exploration for Missing Objects
description: Use this when the specific location of required objects is not provided or immediately visible.
---
Navigate through the environment and inspect potential furniture or storage areas sequentially until the required items are located.

---
name: Sequential Handling of Multiple Items
description: Use this when a task requires collecting multiple instances of the same type of object.
---
Pick up and transport items one by one, ensuring each is successfully deposited at the destination before searching for the next, rather than attempting to gather all items before moving to the destination.

---
name: Consistent Storage Destination
description: Use this when you need to place multiple objects into a specific type of container.
---
Once a valid target container has been identified and opened, utilize the same container for all subsequent items of that type to avoid redundant searching or opening multiple containers.

items.content: After locating and moving the first instance of the required object, continue searching other potential surfaces for additional instances. Do not assume that all required items are in the same location; maintain a systematic search until the full quantity is collected.

items.content: Before moving an item into a container, always verify its state; if it is closed, you must open it first. If you close a container after placing an item, remember to reopen it before attempting to add further items to that same container.

memory_context:
---
name: Cooling Items
description: Use when the task requirement involves "cool [object]".
---
To cool an object, you must place it inside a fridge to change its state. Do not assume that randomly found objects are already at the required temperature; always locate and utilize a fridge to perform the cooling action before attempting to complete the task.

---
name: Action Sequence Planning
description: Use when a task requires multiple state changes (e.g., finding, then cooling, then placing).
---
Break complex tasks into distinct sub-goals: first retrieve the target object, then apply the necessary state transformations (like cooling in a fridge), and finally move the object to the destination. Do not attempt the final placement until the object satisfies all state constraints specified in the query.

---
name: Preventing Redundant Search Loops
description: Use when the agent is stuck repeatedly examining the same objects or visiting empty containers.
---
If you have already inspected a container and found it empty, mark it as searched and avoid revisiting it. If progress stalls, stop re-examining held items and focus on identifying which appliance is needed to modify the object's current state to meet the task's requirements.

---
name: Post-State Change Goal Verification
description: Use this when a task involves preparing an object before moving it to a final location.
---
After completing an intermediate state change (such as heating or cooling an object), explicitly re-check the original objective to verify that the final placement step has not been omitted before finalizing the task.

---
name: Sequence Planning for Multi-Step Tasks
description: Use this when planning tasks that require multiple distinct operations on the same object.
---
Structure the task plan to explicitly include the final placement action as the terminal step, ensuring the agent does not interpret the completion of a preparatory step (like heating) as the end of the entire task.

memory_context:
---
name: Systematic Exploration of the Environment
description: Use this strategy when the initial search for target objects fails to yield results.
---
Instead of repeatedly visiting the same locations, perform an exhaustive and systematic sweep of all furniture and containers listed in the initial room observation to ensure no potential storage spot is overlooked.

---
name: Expanding Search Scope Beyond Primary Furniture
description: Use this when common locations like desks or tables do not contain the required items.
---
Do not limit searches to the most obvious surface; if target items are not found, prioritize checking all other available storage units such as shelves, safes, and secondary tables rather than getting stuck re-checking the same few areas.

---
name: Avoiding Redundant Search Cycles
description: Use this when the agent detects it is repeatedly visiting the same locations without progress.
---
Monitor the search history to identify and break out of search loops, and explicitly force the agent to traverse to unvisited locations to ensure the entire environment is covered.

---
name: Target Specific Objects for Examination
description: Use this strategy when the task requires examining a specific item placed on a surface or within a container.
---
Do not settle for examining the surrounding furniture or surface where the item is located. Always perform the interaction action directly on the target object itself to ensure the system processes the request for the specific item rather than the container.

---
name: Sequencing Tool-Assisted Interactions
description: Use this strategy when a task implies that an object must be interacted with while a specific tool is active.
---
First, ensure the tool is in the necessary active state. Immediately following the tool's activation, execute the requested action directly on the target object, rather than interacting with the environment or the tool itself again.

items.title: Spatial Proximity Requirement
items.description: Use when an instruction specifies performing an action on an object "with" another tool or appliance.
items.content: You must bring both the target object and the tool into the same location or container. Simple activation of a tool in a different location will not satisfy the condition; the agent must be physically adjacent to both items simultaneously during the interaction.

items.title: Prioritizing Portable Object Movement
items.description: Use when an interaction requires a stationary tool (like a heavy lamp) and a movable target object.
items.content: If the required tool is stationary or heavy, transport the target object to the location of the tool rather than attempting to operate the tool remotely. Always evaluate if the target object is pickable before assuming it must remain at its initial location.

items.title: Sequencing Interactions for Correct State
items.description: Use when a task requires an environmental change (like turning on a light) to examine or modify an object.
items.content: Perform the activation of the tool only when the agent and the target object are in the immediate vicinity. If the agent moves to a different location after activation, the interaction effect will be lost; always maintain proximity to the target object while the tool is actively influencing the area.

name: Prioritizing State Changes
description: Use this when a task requires an object to undergo a state change (e.g., cooling) before final placement.
---
Ensure the object undergoes the required state-changing action using the appropriate appliance before transferring it to the final destination. This prevents unnecessary backtracking and re-handling of the object if it was moved to the target location prematurely.

---
name: Sequential Object Searching
description: Use this when the required object is not immediately visible in the initial storage area.
---
If an object is not found in its typical storage location, systematically search adjacent surfaces and alternative containers. Maintain awareness of the search area and expand the range of visited locations until the target object is located.

---
name: Locating Perishable Food Items
description: When tasked with retrieving produce or perishable food, prioritize searching inside refrigeration units first.
---
Refrigerator units are the primary storage locations for fresh food items. If the desired item is not immediately visible in the environment, navigate to the fridge and open it to check for the required object.

---
name: Preparing Appliances for Interaction
description: When placing an item inside an appliance, always ensure the appliance is open before executing the placement action.
---
Many appliances, such as microwaves, are closed by default. You must successfully open the appliance door before you can place an object inside it.

---
name: Conducting Systematic Searches
description: Use when a target object is not immediately found in the most likely locations.
---
Do not rely on checking the same few containers repeatedly. Maintain a mental checklist of unexamined containers and visit them sequentially, ensuring all relevant storage units (cabinets, drawers, appliances) are checked before assuming the object is not present in the environment.
